Our task is to find A, B and C such that

−2x2+21x+41(x+1)(2−x)(x+3)=A(x+1)+B(2−x)+C(x+3).

Multiplying both sides by (x+1)(2−x)(x+3) gives

−2x2+21x+41=A(2−x)(x+3)+B(x+1)(x+3)+C(x+1)(2−x).

For x=−1, we get −2(−1)2+21(−1)+41=A(2−(−1))(−1+3)=+B(−1+1)(−1+3)=+C(−1+1)(2−(−1))−2−21+41=A(6)A=186A=3.

For x=2, we get −2(2)2+21(2)+41=A(2−2)(2+3)=+B(2+1)(2+3)=+C(2+1)(2−2)−8+42+41=B(15)B=7515B=5.

For x=−3, we get −2(−3)2+21(−3)+41=A(2−(−3))(−3+3)=+B(−3+1)(−3+3)=+C(−3+1)(2−(−3))−18−63+41=C(−10)C=−40−10C=4. Hence, −2x2+21x+41(x+1)(2−x)(x+3)=3(x+1)+5(2−x)+4(x+3).

Your Answer:
3(x+1)−2(2−x)+6(x+3)
